releases.name: LinBox Prefix Pack linbox-wine-proton-10.0-arm64ec-bionic (arm64ec)
releases.body:
LinBox v8.4 前缀架构 · 预构建前缀模板包（arm64ec）

- 构建模式: full（full=无头 wineboot 完整 hive；auto=失败降级骨架；skeleton=纯骨架）
- 布局: both（full=秒开模板【--keep-stamp】；component=drive_c.tar.xz + *.reg.xz【arm64ec 不带 directx】）
- bionic 运行时: Android API29 官方镜像提取（真 linker64 + bionic 库）；wineboot 环境与设备端 EnvSupport 同源（rootfs usr/lib → wine lib → /system/lib64）
- 消费方式（三布局）:
  - `*.tar.zst` —— 独立模板包：放入 `rootfs/opt/prefix/pack/`（生态通道，任意 wine 槽位可用）
  - `*-with-wine.tar.gz` —— 槽位树布局：App「Wine 管理 → 从本地安装」（prefix-pack 自动随槽位落位，成为该槽位一级模板来源）
  - `*-with-wine-rootfs.tar.gz` — data/data 全路径：终端 `linbox-container install-wine <包>` 一键落位
- 设备端四级模板来源与供给链详见 `docs/prefix-architecture.md`

releases.name: LinBox Bionic Box64 v0.4.4 (aarch64)
releases.body:
LinBox bionic rootfs 专用 Box64（aarch64 / NDK bionic 链接 / -DANDROID=ON / ARM_DYNAREC）

- bionic ELF（PT_INTERP=/system/bin/linker64），与 rootfs 内
  wine / mesa / pulseaudio 等二进制同链同形态；box64 本体零
  glibc 依赖
- 完整安装集（不再只有单个 box64 执行文件）：
  `usr/local/bin/box64` + `usr/bin/box64` PATH 入口链接
  + `usr/lib/box64-x86_64-linux-gnu/libc++_shared.so`
  （上游 ANDROID 模式配套，被仿真 x86_64 程序的 C++ 标准库）
  + `usr/etc/box64.box64rc`（系统级调优开关）
  + `usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/`（`ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`
  私有加载器与 aarch64 glibc 运行库 —— glibc 形态 box64
  与 rootfs 内 glibc 二进制的运行层）
  + `usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/`（被仿真 x86_64 程序的
  glibc 运行库，box64 经 BOX64_LD_LIBRARY_PATH 查找）
- 手动安装: 解包 `linbox-box64-*.tar.gz` 至 /（data/data/com.linbox/...
  自动就位），或 `linbox-container install-box64 <tar.gz|URL>`
- 安装后 linbox-container 自动探测 /usr/local/bin/box64
- 用途: 在 aarch64 设备上运行 x86_64 Wine（backend=box64）；
  v0.4.4 为 hangover-11.16 官方配套版本（错配可致 wineboot SEH 级联崩溃）
- 注意: 与完整 rootfs 包（build-bionic-rootfs）同源 —— rootfs 已内置
  同款 box64 与配套文件，单独升级时才需要本包

Bayonetta 3 Recomp v0.5.0
releases.body:
A new look for both launchers and the touch controls, and phone vibration.

**New background art** on every launcher: a moonlit balcony over a violet night city.

**Android launcher, redesigned for a phone held sideways**
- A top bar with the title, the version and Follow; Report a bug and Settings on the right.
- Status chips for the game data, shader cache, controller, chip and temperature. Tap one for the details.
- One notice at a time (setup, update, game mode) instead of stacked cards.
- Under your right thumb: a 30 / 40 / 60 performance switch and a big START that stays on screen however short the display.
- The Settings panel fits the screen. New rows: **Phone vibration** and **Show frame rate**.

**Touch controls**: redrawn as dark glass in the launcher's colours, with white labels; a pressed button lights up gold.

**Phone vibration**: with no controller in use, the game's rumble now vibrates the phone itself, softer than full strength. With a controller in use, its own motors rumble as before. Turn it off under Settings > Phone vibration.

**Frame-rate counter**: now off by default on Android, as on desktop. Turn it on under Settings > Show frame rate.

> **Follow the author on X: [@aoxzh](https://x.com/aoxzh)** for progress updates, previews and new releases.

## What's new

### Android: 1080p (docked) resolution
Phones always ran the game in handheld mode at 1280×720, and there was no way to change it. **Settings > Resolution** now offers:
- **Handheld · 720p**: the default, and the lighter of the two.
- **Docked · 1080p**: the game draws as it does on a TV, at up to 1600×900, shown at 1080p.

Docked mode is sharper but much heavier on the GPU, the battery and the heat. Try it on a strong phone. It takes effect the next time the game starts.

- **From v0.4.4:** use **Update now** in the launcher (Android: then tap **SET UP** again).
- **From an older version:** desktop, unpack over the old install and choose **Rebuild**; Android, install the APK over the old app.

releases.name: Bayonetta 3 Recomp v0.4.4
releases.body:
> **Follow the author on X: [@aoxzh](https://x.com/aoxzh)** for progress updates, previews and new releases.

## What's new

### One-click updates
- **Windows / Linux / Steam Deck:** when a newer release is out, the launcher shows **Update now** on the home screen and in its menu, so a controller can reach it. One click:
  1. Downloads the release.
  2. Checks it against the release's sha256.
  3. Replaces the program files.
  4. Restarts the launcher and rebuilds the game.

  Your settings, saves, game data and mods (everything under `private/`) stay.
- **Android:** **Update now** downloads the new APK inside the app and opens Android's installer. Android checks the signature before installing. Afterwards the launcher asks you to tap **SET UP** again; it continues from the last setup and only rebuilds what changed.
- Nothing is downloaded without that tap. **Settings > Check for updates** turns the check off.

### New icon
- New art for the app, the launchers, the shortcuts and the README.

## Updating to this version
- **Windows / Linux / Steam Deck:** unpack the release over the old one, then choose **Rebuild**. This is the last time you need to update by hand.

### Better bug reports

> [!NOTE]
Wondering about your save data when upgrading? Don't worry! Your save data is stored separately to the game itself. You can overwrite your old version and your save data will still be there, completely intact, and will work on the new version.

### Changelog
- Collected Jinjos will be now be permanently saved when collected, just like Notes. A new option has been added to choose only saving Jinjos or Notes if desired. The new default behavior will be to save both Notes and Jinjos as present in the Xbox 360 version of the game. Special thanks to @wedarobi for their work on this major feature!
- Fixed a major memory leak that would occur on MacOS by updating RT64. The game should now be significantly more stable on extended play sessions on Mac.

releases.name: Cemu Plus 0.4.1
releases.body:
Android build of Cemu Plus, a fork of the Cemu Android port with Lossless Scaling frame generation.

## What's new

### Game updates
- **Use update** in the settings of a game, under Update, turns its installed update off, and the game runs as its base version. It's only shown for games with an update, and applies the next time the game starts. The game card shows the version the game runs as
- Games whose update doesn't work in Cemu have it off by default, with a note under the switch saying it's recommended off. **Why?** opens the reason

### Fixes
- ZombiU no longer stays on a black screen after the Ubisoft logo. Its update (v32) doesn't work in Cemu, so it's off by default and ZombiU runs as its base version


## Frame generation setup
1. Copy `Lossless.dll` from your own copy of Lossless Scaling (its installation folder on Windows) to your device.
2. In Cemu Plus open **Settings → Graphics settings → Frame generation (Lossless Scaling)** and tap **Select Lossless.dll**.
3. Enable frame generation there or from the in-game menu, where the multiplier, target frame rate and motion estimation resolution can be changed while playing.

releases.name: Cemu Plus 0.4.0
releases.body:
Android build of Cemu Plus, a fork of the Cemu Android port with Lossless Scaling frame generation.

## What's new

### Motion sensitivity
- **Motion sensitivity X axis** and **Motion sensitivity Y axis** set how fast turning left and right, and tilting up and down go, from 25% to 500%. They are next to the motion inversion on each controller's page in **Input settings** and in the quick menu under Controls, and work for the motion of the device and of controllers
- They scale the turning speed the game gets, which is what aiming with motion uses. A tilt that is held still settles at the real angle of the device

### Updated to the latest Cemu
Cemu Plus now includes everything the main Cemu project added since April 2026:
- **Wii U CPU on ARM:** fixes in the ARM64 recompiler that runs every game, for single-precision float stores (now faster too), division by zero, carry flags and a few wrong instructions. The default NaN mode of ARM is turned off to match the Wii U
- **Performance:** smaller Vulkan and GPU optimizations, like checking only the render state that changed, caching shader lookups and using the fast draw path more often

releases.body:
Android build of Cemu Plus, a fork of the Cemu Android port with Lossless Scaling frame generation.

## Frame generation setup
1. Copy `Lossless.dll` from your own copy of Lossless Scaling (its installation folder on Windows) to your device.
2. In Cemu Plus open **Settings → Graphics settings → Frame generation (Lossless Scaling)** and tap **Select Lossless.dll**.
3. Enable frame generation there or from the in-game menu, where the multiplier, target frame rate and motion estimation resolution can be changed while playing.

Frame generation requires the Vulkan memory model, float16 and null descriptor support from the GPU driver.
The FPS overlay shows the displayed frame rate together with the base frame rate while frame generation is active.

**Full changelog:** [v0.3.5...v0.3.6-beta.2](https://github.com/danielcamilo1/cemu-plus/compare/v0.3.5...v0.3.6-beta.2)

releases.name: Underground 1 Android Evolved v0.2.15
releases.body:
## Underground 1 Android Evolved v0.2.15: más rendimiento

### Cambios

- **Más rendimiento en procesadores con 2 núcleos rápidos** (Helio G85/G88/G99, MT6769/MT6789 y similares). En la versión anterior dejamos de fijar los hilos del juego a los núcleos rápidos en estos procesadores, y en algunos volvió el lag. Ahora el hilo principal del juego, el que más trabaja, va en los núcleos rápidos, y los demás hilos los reparte Android. Con 4 o más núcleos rápidos no cambia nada: todos los hilos van en ellos.
- **Menos trabajo inútil en cada fotograma.** El juego pregunta por `d3d9.dll` en cada fotograma, y el port lo anotaba en el registro cada vez: unas 2000 líneas por segundo en Most Wanted y Carbon. Ahora se anota una sola vez. Otras líneas repetitivas (texturas convertidas en la CPU, entrada de teclado, liberación de superficies) también se limitan. Además de ahorrar CPU, el registro de los reportes conserva lo importante.

Dos APK: **arm64** y **armeabi-v7a**. Android 10+, Vulkan 1.1+. Misma firma; se instalan como actualización. Se adjunta `NFSU1-v0.2.15-SHA256SUMS.txt`.

releases.name: Underground 1 Android Evolved v0.2.14
releases.body:
## Underground 1 Android Evolved v0.2.14: rendimiento recuperado

### Cambios

- **Rendimiento recuperado en procesadores con solo 2 núcleos rápidos** (Helio G85/G88, MT6769 y similares). Desde la versión anterior, todos los hilos del juego se fijaban a los núcleos rápidos. En estos procesadores eso los metía todos en solo 2 núcleos, y el juego iba peor que antes. Ahora solo se fijan cuando hay al menos 4 núcleos rápidos; si no, Android los reparte como antes.
- **Reportes más completos.** Se guardan las tres últimas sesiones del registro del juego, no solo dos: muchos jugadores reabren el juego un par de veces tras un cierre antes de reportar, y la sesión del cierre se perdía. En el resumen del issue, las trazas del cierre van abreviadas para que quepan más líneas del juego.

Dos APK: **arm64** y **armeabi-v7a**. Android 10+, Vulkan 1.1+. Misma firma; se instalan como actualización. Se adjunta `NFSU1-v0.2.14-SHA256SUMS.txt`.

releases.name: Underground 1 Android Evolved v0.2.13
releases.body:
## Underground 1 Android Evolved v0.2.13: driver recomendado para tu GPU

### Driver Vulkan recomendado para tu procesador

- **El launcher te dice qué driver usar.** En *Opciones › Driver Vulkan* ahora aparece la GPU de tu teléfono y el driver que le conviene:
  - **Snapdragon (Adreno 6xx/7xx):** Turnip (Mesa), si el driver del sistema va lento o con errores gráficos.
  - **MediaTek, Exynos, Tensor o Unisoc con Mali-G57 o más nueva:** PanVK (Mesa), con la misma condición.
  - **Mali-G52/G72/G76 o más antiguas:** el driver del sistema (PanVK aún es experimental en ellas).
  - **PowerVR (Moto g54, Helio G35/G37…) y Samsung Xclipse:** el driver del sistema. No hay un driver alternativo que funcione en ellas.
- **Aviso si el driver no es para tu GPU.** Si eliges un driver hecho para otra GPU (por ejemplo, Turnip en una Mali o PanVK en una Adreno), el launcher avisa de que el juego probablemente no arrancará.

La app no incluye ningún driver: los importas tú como ZIP (adrenotools) desde el mismo diálogo.

Dos APK: **arm64** y **armeabi-v7a**. Android 10+, Vulkan 1.1+. Misma firma; se instalan como actualización. Se adjunta `NFSU1-v0.2.13-SHA256SUMS.txt`. Incluye todo lo de la v0.2.12.

releases.name: Underground 1 Android Evolved v0.2.12
releases.body:
## Underground 1 Android Evolved v0.2.12: volver al juego sin cierres y reportes completos

### Correcciones

- **Cierre al volver al juego.** Si salías a otra app y volvías, el juego podía cerrarse en el primer fotograma. Android libera la ventana del juego al pasar a segundo plano, pero la superficie Vulkan seguía usándola y se destruía después. Ahora la superficie conserva su ventana hasta que se destruye.

### Reportes más útiles

- **El resumen del issue ya trae las líneas del juego.** Antes se tomaban de logcat y, cuando pulsabas *Reportar*, Android ya las había borrado: casi todos los issues llegaban con "últimas líneas del juego" vacío. Ahora salen del registro propio del juego (`game.log`), y logcat solo aporta las líneas del cierre.
- **Lecturas de archivo incompletas en el registro.** Si el juego pide más datos de los que recibe de un archivo, se anota el archivo, la posición y su tamaño. Así podremos ver si un cierre viene de un archivo del juego dañado o incompleto.

### Ajustes para teléfonos con GPU débil

releases.name: Underground 1 Android Evolved v0.2.11
releases.body:
## Underground 1 Android Evolved v0.2.11: mega actualización

Revisamos los reportes y los zip de diagnóstico que nos enviaron. Esta versión trae las mismas mejoras de fondo que Most Wanted y Underground 2.

### Estabilidad

- **Lecturas de archivos completas.** En algunos teléfonos, Android entregaba los archivos del juego a trozos y el juego tomaba un archivo a medias por uno completo, lo que podía cerrar el juego al cargar. Ahora se lee hasta el final.
- **Protección para GPU PowerVR (MediaTek, p. ej. Moto g54 / Dimensity 7020).** El driver Vulkan de MediaTek se caía al crear el primer pipeline gráfico. Ahora, si el driver falla, el port reintenta con configuraciones más simples hasta encontrar una que funcione. *No hemos podido probarlo en un teléfono PowerVR; si tienes uno, cuéntanos cómo va.*

### Audio

- **Menos saturación.** El mezclador ya no corta el sonido en seco cuando se suman muchos sonidos; ahora lo comprime con suavidad.

### Rendimiento

- **Hilos del juego en los núcleos rápidos.** Se fijan a los núcleos grandes y se le indica a Android cuánto dura cada fotograma (ADPF).

### Controles

- **El botón A del mando también hace Enter** mientras conduces.

# Heaven Dust no Android — v0.1 (experimental)

Primeira release do port. Launcher v9 (versionCode 10, jogo 1.0.2).

## O que já funciona (testado no Galaxy S23)

- O jogo abre e roda com a tradução PT-BR 1.1 aplicada e confirmada dentro do jogo
- Porter 8/8: 2.924 / 2.924 shaders traduzidos para Vulkan
- Launcher próprio: importação do data pack, escolha de driver de GPU (incl. Turnip), 3 modos de tela (Fit / Stretch / Crop) no launcher e no menu de pausa, música tema com botão mudo

## O que ainda NÃO foi provado

- Jogar do início ao fim — até agora só a abertura e a tradução foram confirmadas no aparelho
- Números de desempenho / FPS, e se o Turnip realmente fica carregado dentro do jogo

## Importante

- O APK sozinho NÃO é o jogo. Você precisa gerar os seus próprios dados com o porter do nx2android, a partir do seu próprio dump (NSP) e das suas próprias chaves — nunca baixe nem compartilhe RomFS, NSP, shaders ou chaves de terceiros.
- Copie os dados soltos para `Android/data/org.nx2a.t010059100d928000/files/`. Se desinstalar o app, o Android apaga essa pasta inteira (dados e saves).
- Esta release NÃO contém arquivos do jogo, chaves, data pack nem shaders.

releases.body:
## 4.0.4 - November 3, 2026
* **The left analog stick now moves the pointer in the menus**, on every controller, like a mouse. It no longer also steps through the buttons; the D-pad still does
* **A Wiimote with anything plugged into it is now always vertical in the menus**, and its buttons and IR pointer work alongside the extension (a Nunchuk on Wii and a Classic Controller on both Wii and Wii U previously lost them)
* **Redesigned Button Mappings screen.** One screen now replaces the separate controller and button screens, showing each button on a drawing of the controller and letting you choose a button by pressing it or from a list.
* **Redesigned Saves screen.** The Save, Load and Delete buttons are now a single **Saves** button. Snapshots fill a grid, with the game's **Cartridge Save** (shown only for games that have one) in its own card beneath. Choosing a card opens a small popover of what can be done with it; the save file's backups are listed from its popover. The Auto Load, Auto Save and Append Auto settings are replaced by a single **Save Mode**: **Snapshot** (the default), **Cartridge Save**, or **Manual**.

releases.name: 4.0.3 - October 20, 2026
releases.body:
* **New menu look!** The menus have been rebuilt with a fresh, modern style: a deeper red header and footer, cleaner rounded buttons with soft shadows, a redesigned game list with a slimmer scrollbar and a clear highlight on the selected entry, new prompt windows, and more. The menu graphics are now drawn procedurally by the renderer instead of being loaded from PNG images, so they stay sharp at any output resolution
* **New controller status bar** in the menu footer, replacing the Wiimote battery icons. Each of the four player slots (P1-P4) now shows the type of controller connected (Wiimote, GameCube controller, etc.), with the battery level shown for Wiimote controllers and the Gamepad. Empty slots appear dimmed
* Wii U: Japanese/Korean/Chinese fonts are now also found in `fceugx/` or `wiiu/apps/fceugx/` on the SD card even before settings have been saved, and stay crisp at 1080p
* Wii U: fix texture reuse causing cover art issues with varying image sizes

  * Output up to 1080p, with a new GPU-powered **ScaleFX** upscaler shader and a **Sharp Bilinear** shader, plus a scanline shader

releases.name: v0.2.26
releases.body:
Smoother frames, drivers for more Adreno phones, GPL-3.0.

## English

**Improved**
- Smoother and lighter frames: the graphics commands are prepared on a separate thread, and the GPU is kept from dropping its clock while frames run late.
- ⚙ frame rate limit now applies at once, no restart. With the 30 fps limit the screen also switches to 60 Hz, which saves battery.
- Snapdragon phones on the system (stock) graphics driver: lighter drawing, the GPU no longer saves and reloads parts of the frame nobody needs.
- New frame counter with a small dot on its left: green = cool, yellow = the phone starts to slow down from heat, red = it is throttling hard.

**Drivers**
- Adreno GPUs that report a two-digit model (for example Retroid Pocket G2) now get the bundled Turnip drivers; before, all of them were hidden.
- Drivers… → new switch "Allow drivers this phone does not support" (off by default): lets you try a driver package the port would normally reject.
- Mali with the PanVK driver: textures are now unpacked by the game itself, the same way as with the phone's own driver.

**License:** the port is now under GPL-3.0-or-later (it includes code from projects under the GPL).

releases.name: v0.2.24
releases.body:
Text input fix, frame output setting, lighter textures on Mali and PowerVR.

## English

**New**
- ⚙ → "Frame output on its own thread": Auto / On / Off (applies on next launch). Auto works as in 0.2.22: on, and switched off by itself only if that thread really crashes twice. The phone closing the game to save battery does not count.

**Fixed**
- Naming a hero: OK no longer stays grey with "finish choosing characters" while the cursor is at the end of the name (Gboard, SwiftKey and other Latin keyboards).

**Improved**
- Mali and PowerVR phones: textures are unpacked on the GPU with a checked decoder and kept in a compact format, so they take less video memory. Nothing changes on Snapdragon (Adreno).
- If the graphics driver fails, the log now says why, which helps fix such crashes.

**Install:** installs over any earlier version and keeps your saves; no setup re-run needed. Android 10 or 11: `Diablo3-Mobile-v0.2.24-arm64-android10.apk`.

## Русский

**Новое**

releases.name: v0.2.23
releases.body:
Faster drawing on Mali and PowerVR.

## English

**Improved**
- Mali and PowerVR phones: the lighter way of drawing from the test build 0.2.11-test4 is now in the release (#4). The GPU skips saving and reloading parts of the frame nobody needs and waits less between drawing steps. Testers on Helio G99 and Dimensity 7050 went from about 30 to 45–60 fps. Nothing changes on Snapdragon (Adreno).
- Everything from 0.2.22 stays: camera zoom-out, LAN play, the newer drivers.

**Install:** installs over any earlier version and keeps your saves; no setup re-run needed. Android 10 or 11: `Diablo3-Mobile-v0.2.23-arm64-android10.apk`.

## Русский

**Улучшено**
- Телефоны на Mali и PowerVR: более лёгкая отрисовка из тестовой сборки 0.2.11-test4 теперь в релизе (#4). Видеокарта не сохраняет и не перечитывает ненужные части кадра и меньше ждёт между этапами отрисовки. У тестеров на Helio G99 и Dimensity 7050 было около 30 fps, стало 45–60. На Snapdragon (Adreno) ничего не меняется.
- Всё из 0.2.22 на месте: отдаление камеры, игра по локальной сети, новые драйверы.

releases.name: v0.2.22
releases.body:
Camera zoom-out, smoother frame delivery.

## English

**New**
- ⚙ → "Camera zoom-out" (100–140 %, changes live): moves the camera back to show more around the hero, at the same angle; the interface keeps its size (#31). 100 % = as on the Switch, about 120 % = as far as on the PC. More of the world on the screen means more GPU load.

**Improved**
- Frames are handed to the screen on a separate thread, so the game's main graphics thread has more time for the next frame. This helps most where the CPU is the limit (a hot phone, slower CPUs). If this ever makes the game crash, the port switches it off by itself after the second such crash.
- A fix for how the game's threads end.

**Install:** no new game patches, no setup re-run needed. Android 10 or 11: `Diablo3-Mobile-v0.2.22-arm64-android10.apk`.

## Русский

**Новое**
- ⚙ → «Отдаление камеры» (100–140 %, меняется сразу): камера отъезжает назад, и вокруг героя видно больше, угол тот же; интерфейс прежнего размера (#31). 100 % — как на Switch, около 120 % — как на ПК. Чем больше мира на экране, тем выше нагрузка на GPU.

**Улучшено**

# 0.60.1 is out

There was a bug in the AppImage Updater Code. To fix this i have to revert to the old AppImage build and wait several weeks to ensure a smooth update process.

# 0.60.0 is out 🎉

This release is special for me. I build emuze with web technologies because that’s where I have the most experience, and I’m really proud of what I’ve achieved over the years. I’ve always wanted to help out in this wonderful emulation community, but aside from testing, I couldn’t do much to help with the emulators I love because I struggled with C++ code, which most emulators are written in. But sometimes you feel forced to try and try again. Since v0.59.0, I’ve successfully added a [change to RMG](https://github.com/Rosalie241/RMG/pull/518) to use the SDL GUID to identify a gamepad more reliably, and I forked Mednafen with [mednafen-sdl3](https://github.com/bmsuseluda/mednafen-sdl3) to greatly expand gamepad support. Those changes are just baby steps in the grand scheme of things, but they felt great, and I hope I can build on them in the future.

# 0.59.2 is out 🎉

This release is mostly preparation work to greatly reduce the file size of the AppImage with release 0.60.0.
Besides this fuse2 is not necessary anymore and Metainfos for AppImage Managers e.g. AM are included.

Please let me know what you think of it in the [emuze discord](https://discord.gg/tCzK7kc6Y4).

## 💥 Features
- added AppImage Metainfos
- AppImage works without fuse2
- Preparation work to greatly reduce the file size of the AppImage with release 0.60.0

# 0.59.0 is out 🎉

As you might now i love the simplicity of console gaming. You start the game and it just works. With emulation more often then not you have to provide more then just the game. You need things like a BIOS file, firmware or key files. I wanted to assist with this for a long time. With this release you can choose a folder where you can put your BIOS files and emuze will pick them up and configure the Emulators. Of course emuze will tell you if a required file is missing. On top of this emuze comes bundled with open source BIOS implementations for PlayStation, Game Boy Advance and NEO GEO. Of course you can use official BIOS files instead if you need by putting them in the BIOS folder. Sadly i was not able to achieve the same result for more complicated systems like PlayStation 3, WiiU and Switch. These systems require a installation of a firmware. I will try to tackle these in a future release.

Besides this i bundled and pre configured ScummVM and DOSBox Pure Unleashed.
Therefore the day is finally here: All 35 supported systems are pre configured and bundled now 🥳

# 0.58.0 is out 🎉

As one of the few nerdy kids in a small sleepy town in a country where arcade gaming was classified as gambling i could see lightgun games in magazines only. I had an NES and Captain N with his Zapper was sooo awesome to me. But when the time came that i could buy one with my own money the rise of flat panels began and with it the death of CRT TVs and Lightguns altogether. It was just a thing of the past, sadly.
But surprisingly the genre came back with the Wii and PS3 and there Pointer devices. Some years later camera based Lightguns came to the market and finally Lightgun gaming with the same and even higher precision is possible on flat panels.

releases.name: Disco Elysium port v0.10.0
releases.body:
## No more blinking objects after loading

While the game is running, each new combination of shader and render state needs a GPU pipeline. Pipelines the app has never seen are built in the background so the game doesn't freeze, and until one is ready the objects that use it are not drawn. Until now that also happened to pipelines it had already built in an earlier session. Only the first 4,000 were prepared at start-up, in the order they first appeared, so later in the game whole areas came from the background again. The result was objects and textures blinking for a few frames after loading a save or when walking into an area.

- Pipelines that the app has already built on your device are now created on the spot, in about a quarter of a millisecond each and within a small per-frame budget, so they are drawn from the first frame.
- Start-up preparation now begins with the pipelines your last session used (`pipelines_recientes.bin` in the game folder), not with the ones from the beginning of the game.
- Areas you visit for the very first time can still show an object a moment late while its pipeline is built. The second visit is clean.

releases.name: Dual-Screen 3.0.2 (based on Dusklight v2.0.0)
releases.body:
Restores compatibility with third-party native mods. If mods failed to load, or loaded and then force-closed the game, this is the fix.

### Fixed

* **Mods failed to load with "Unknown mod load failure".** ([#6](https://github.com/igawa6/dusklight/issues/6))

  Adding the companion's slot I/II buttons pushed `BTN_R` to `1 << 8` and widened `daAlink_c::itemTriggerCheck` / `itemButtonCheck` from `u8` to `u16`. That changes the mangled names, so mods built against upstream Dusklight could not resolve them and failed at `dlopen`. The upstream symbols are re-exported as forwarders that translate the button numbering as well as the width — upstream's `BTN_B` is `BTN_S2` here, so widening alone would have routed a sword check to a slot button.

  Measured against three mods: only 2 of 842, 762 and 55 game-symbol imports were unresolved.

* **The game force-closed when a loaded mod ran.**

releases.name: Dual-Screen 3.0.1 (based on Dusklight v2.0.0)
releases.body:
Patch release for **Dual-Screen 3.0**. No gameplay or dual-screen changes — the native code is identical to 3.0.

### Fixed

* **Cosmetics, Luau Support and Randomizer were missing from the Android build.** ([#6](https://github.com/igawa6/dusklight/issues/6))

  The Android CMake presets listed only the `dusklight` target, so the `dusklight_mods` aggregate target never ran and `bundled_mods/` was never produced. Gradle packs that directory into `assets/mods`, so the APK shipped with no bundled mod packages at all. Mods that depend on the Luau runtime could not load either.

  All three packages are now present: `cosmetics`, `luau_runtime` and `randomizer`.

  CI was never affected — `build.yml` builds `dusklight_mods` as its own explicit `--target` step. This only broke preset-driven local builds.

App Store: 1.2.0 (124), bundle games.bachatas4, interpreter only.

## New

  "Native Metal renderer (Experimental)". It applies from the next game launch. MoltenVK stays
  the default renderer. Metal has been tested on Bloodborne only. Some games may render wrongly or not start with Metal; switch it off if so.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.5.3 (beta 49): profundidade de 16 bits, para os Huawei Maleoon
releases.body:
**Beta 49.** Uma opção nova para o formato da profundidade das sombras, que deve resolver as cenas escuras nos Huawei Maleoon.

> **Vindo da 0.5.2, não precisa compilar o código do jogo de novo**: é só instalar por cima. De versões anteriores, a tela inicial pede uma vez.

## Profundidade de 16 bits (#516, #240)

O jogo guarda a profundidade dos mapas de sombra em 16 bits (D16). O driver dos Huawei Maleoon recusava o D16 e fechava o jogo na abertura (#301). Por isso, desde a 0.4.0, o app usava D32 nesses aparelhos. Só que o D32 deixa cenas inteiras escuras: o céu fica certo, mas o terreno, as construções e os personagens quase pretos (#516). No POCO F7 Ultra, forçando o D32, a mesma cena ficou com metade do brilho.

- **Opção nova:** tela inicial > Compatibilidade do driver > **Profundidade de 16 bits (sombras)**: Automático, D16, D32 ou D24.
- **Automático nos Maleoon agora é D24**, e D32 só se o driver não aceitar o D24. No POCO, o D24 sai praticamente igual ao D16. Nas outras GPUs nada muda: continua D16.
- Se um formato não puder ser usado para tudo nesse driver, o app troca por outro que possa, e o log diz qual.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.5.2 (beta 48): mods de código
releases.body:
**Beta 48.** Mods que trazem código agora funcionam, e mais um crash com os alvos da Pedra Sheikah foi coberto.

> **Precisa compilar o código do jogo de novo, uma vez:** a tela inicial pede depois de instalar.

## Mods de código (#390)

Até aqui o app usava só a pasta `romfs` dos mods, que guarda arquivos do jogo, como textos, texturas e modelos. Agora ele também usa a pasta `exefs`, como o Eden, o Yuzu e o Ryujinx:

- **Patches IPS do código do jogo** (`exefs/<build id>.ips`, IPS ou IPS32): entram no código do jogo quando ele é compilado.
- **Módulos extras** (`exefs/subsdk1` a `subsdk9`, como os feitos com exlaunch): também são compilados e ficam logo depois do código do jogo, onde o Switch os coloca.

Funciona nos modos **Recompilado** e **Nativo**. O teste foi com a tradução árabe Arabic_Hesham, que forma as letras árabes e põe o texto da direita para a esquerda com o próprio código: a tela de título e os menus saem em árabe.

Como usar:
- Em Configurações > Mods > **Importar pasta de mod**, escolha a pasta do mod, a que tem `romfs` e/ou `exefs` dentro. A tela de Mods ainda fala só em `romfs`, mas as duas são importadas.

O jogo guarda o alvo do Magnesis e da câmera da Pedra Sheikah. Às vezes, esse alvo é um ator que já tinha sumido, e o jogo lia a memória dele e fechava. No log isso aparecia como `accessing 0x...3f800570 in the game's code` em `main+120bc44`, na Mali e no Adreno.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.5.0 (beta 46): amiibo
releases.body:
**Beta 46.** Agora dá para usar amiibo no jogo, sem figura física, e os menus ficaram mais fáceis de usar com o dedo.

## amiibo (#181)

Um leitor de amiibo virtual, com as 36 figuras que o jogo reconhece: as da série Zelda, o Lobo Link, e as de outras séries que dão itens.

- **Como usar:** escolha a runa amiibo e aponte para onde os itens vão cair. Depois toque **de novo no botão da runa** (no layout clássico, o L): o menu abre já na escolha do amiibo, em Controles. Escolha a figura e toque em **Encostar o amiibo**. O menu fecha e o jogo lê a figura.
- Com um controle, ou fora da runa: abra o menu e vá em Controles > amiibo.
- Cada figura dá seus itens uma vez por dia, como no Switch. Os dados de cada figura ficam salvos no app: o coração e o progresso do Lobo Link continuam entre as partidas.

## Menus no toque

- **As listas rolam com o dedo**, com inércia, inclusive as que abrem (como a de amiibo): antes era preciso arrastar uma barra de rolagem fina. As barras e os puxadores também ficaram maiores.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.13 (beta 45): correção para o travamento da Mali nas lutas
releases.body:
**Beta 45.** Uma correção para o travamento depois de alguns minutos de luta na Mali, e três mudanças de desempenho para a Mali.

## O travamento da Mali (#401)

Na Mali-G1 Ultra do #401, o jogo travava depois de alguns minutos de luta (com muitos efeitos), no modo Nativo e no Recompilado. Os logs mostravam uma thread do jogo presa percorrendo a lista de blocos livres do alocador de memória do jogo, que dava a volta.

- **A causa provável:** na Mali, o que um shader grava na memória do jogo é copiado de volta quando a GPU termina. Fora da "arena" de memória global, essa cópia era da faixa inteira, e desfazia o que o jogo tinha escrito ali no meio-tempo, inclusive os cabeçalhos e os links da lista de blocos livres, que ficam logo antes dos buffers. A 0.4.10 já fazia a cópia certa, mas só dentro da arena, que nunca liga nas Malis cujo driver oferece a importação de memória (como a G1 Ultra).
- **O que muda:** agora volta só o que a GPU mudou, palavra por palavra, e o que o jogo escreveu no meio-tempo fica. Quando isso acontece, o log diz `copy-back: a word the game wrote meanwhile kept`.

# PokePark 2: Wonders Beyond, PC and Android port (beta) 0.2.0

No game data is included: you need your own copy of the game (USA, S2LE01).

## Downloads

- **Windows** (10 or 11, 64-bit; Vulkan 1.3 or OpenGL 3.3): unzip and run PokePark2.exe. Keep the prompts and tools folders, SDL3.dll and vcruntime140.dll beside it. If you're updating, unzip over your old folder; your saves and settings stay.
- **Android** (11 or later, arm64, Vulkan 1.3): install PokePark2.apk over the previous version. Your saves stay.

## What's new

- **Languages.** Options > Gameplay > Language. English is built in. For Japanese, French, German, Italian or Spanish, choose it, then Language pack: it asks for your Japanese (S2LJ01) or European (S2LP01) disc image and makes a language pack from it. The game still runs from the USA disc. The port's own menus are translated too.
- **Audio options.** Options > Audio: music, sound effects and voices volumes, and the voices' language (English, Japanese, French or German), chosen apart from the text's.
- **Controls overhaul.**
  - Menus and minigames can be bound apart from the park.
  - Inverted look, stick dead zone and stick speed.

What's new in 0.78

For players
- **32-bit devices:** one APK now holds both ARMv8 (arm64-v8a) and ARMv7
  (armeabi-v7a). Android picks the right one on install, so 64-bit devices
  always run the 64-bit version. OpenGL ES 3.0 is still required.
- **Screen orientation:** the setting now applies to the launcher as well as
  the game and takes effect at once. Auto respects the system rotation lock.
- **Sound:** the audio buffer margin now adapts to the device.
- **Launcher:** new Advanced screen with a Debug mode switch. With it off,
  nothing is written to the log.
- **Logs:** new screen under Data to export, share or send logs to the
  developer, or clear them.

Under the hood
- **Most of the game is now ported C++:** - game code is moving from recompiled to ported native ARM code.
- **Old processor code removed:** x87 emulation is gone from the generated
  code, and the whole game runs in 24-bit floating point. MMX, CPU detection
  and the Pentium FDIV workarounds are removed too.

Known limits
- ARMv7 has only been tested in the 32-bit mode of a 64-bit phone, not on a
  real 32-bit device, so speed on older hardware is unknown.

releases.body:
# Open Nectar 1.0.9.1 — Windows antivirus fix

### **Windows only.** 

Linux, macOS and Android stay on
[1.0.9](https://github.com/SSunnKing/Open-Nectar---Pikmin-Native-PC-Mobile-Port/releases/tag/1.0.9).
Download those from there. Nothing changes in the games themselves.

**Updating:** press **Update** in your launcher. Saves, settings and texture
packs carry over.

## Windows Defender flagged the launcher as a trojan

Some players got a "Threat found" warning from Windows Defender for
`nectar-launcher.exe` (`Trojan:Win32/Bearfoos.A!ml`). This was a false
positive. The `!ml` means it came from Defender's machine-learning guess,
not from a real malware match.

The launcher was doing things that look suspicious to an antivirus: it
started `curl.exe` and `tar.exe` in the background to download updates and
texture packs, and the exe had no publisher or version info. This release
changes that:

* Downloads now happen inside the launcher instead of through `curl.exe`.
* Update zips are unpacked inside the launcher instead of through `tar.exe`.
* `nectar.exe`, `nectar-pal.exe` and `nectar-launcher.exe` now have
  publisher and version information (right-click → Properties → Details).

## New in 1.0

- **Less work for the GPU**: fewer drawing passes per frame (clears are folded into the next pass, empty depth passes are gone) and depth and stencil that a pass does not change are no longer written back to memory. This helps most on Mali and older Adreno phones. If objects go missing or flicker after updating, add `DM_VK_LAZY_CLEAR=0` to env.txt and tell us in an issue.
- **A crash risk removed**: a diagnostic that sampled the game during loads could, rarely, break the game's own code at that moment. It is now off and made safe (it closed Legends: Arceus at start in v0.99).

On Android some of them filled up, and the game then used memory it never got and closed. That was the Dynamax crash, the crash when changing the first Pokémon in your team, and several other crashes in the middle of play. # Swap2-Native 0.2.0.2-beta

Less memory trouble in heavy places, a clearer "Compiling shaders" screen, and Pokémon Pokopia's shader update made short.

**Install over 0.2.0.1-beta.** Games, packs, mods, saves and shader libraries are kept, and nothing is prepared again.

## Fixed

- **A game that slows to a crawl when the phone runs out of memory** (Zelda: Ocarina of Time entering Castle Town on a 16 GB phone fell to under 1 fps for minutes). The texture cache now notices when the phone starts swapping the game out and stops growing instead. If a game still stutters in big areas, turn on **RAM saving** (Game settings) and close other apps.
- **Zelda: Ocarina of Time on phones with 12 GB of RAM or less** uses less memory for textures and graphics memory (from Banana Native).
- **The "Compiling shaders" screen** shows its whole text on two lines (the time left and "Tap to skip" were cut off), and its bar follows the count.
- **Pokémon Pokopia** updates its shaders quickly after installing 0.2.0: about 60 shaders instead of all of them.

releases.name: Swap2-Native 0.2.0.1-beta
releases.body:
# Swap2-Native 0.2.0.1-beta

A fix for 0.2.0-beta: no more black screen while a game prepares its pipelines.

**Install over 0.2.0-beta.** Games, packs, mods, saves and shader libraries are kept, and nothing is translated or prepared again.

## Fixed

- **A black screen at the first start of a game** (seen with Turnip drivers, for example on a Redmagic 11 Air). Since 0.2.0, a game prepares its known pipelines before it plays (at most 90 seconds). The loading screen had already gone by then, so the game looked stuck. Now the loading screen stays and shows **Compiling shaders: N of M**; tap it to skip the rest. On Turnip the pipelines are made one at a time, so the first start takes the full 90 seconds unless you skip; the next starts are short.

Everything else is as in [0.2.0-beta](https://github.com/mamcjr/Swap2-Native/releases/tag/v0.2.0-beta).

## Thanks

**moceure and the Banana Native contributors**, **enjoyerofslop / DroidPlay Core**, **Sergii "iOrange" Kudlai** (bcdec), **erickmendes22** and **EddizEge / AnkaNative**. Licenses and attribution are included in the sources.

releases.name: Swap2-Native 0.2.0-beta
releases.body:
# Swap2-Native 0.2.0-beta

Five more Switch 2 games boot, Zelda: Ocarina of Time draws its grass and gets faster, and a new graphics menu offers four upscalers with a level, plus grass and fog options.

**Install over 0.1.9.3-beta.** Games, packs, mods and saves are kept. **The shaders change:** each game updates its shader library the first time you play it after installing. Only the shaders that changed are translated again, so in most games the update is short (Ocarina of Time about 2,300). It takes longer in **Yoshi and the Mysterious Book** (about 40,000), and two games translate all of their shaders again: **Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave** (about 17,000) and **Pokémon Pokopia** (about 131,000, which takes hours; keep the phone charging). While a game updates, its earlier shaders keep it playable. **Games you already prepared also prepare their code again once** (the "rewrite" step of Prepare; Mario Kart World takes about an hour and a half on a POCO F7 Ultra): keep the app in front until it is done.

## New

# Swap2-Native 0.1.9.3-beta

Swap2-Native now speaks the Switch 2's 16 languages, works with a controller from the library to the in-game panel, has a redesigned in-game panel, and offers a frame rate cap in every game.

**Install over 0.1.9.1-beta (or any 0.1.5-beta and later).** Games, packs, mods and saves are kept. The shaders do not change.

## New

- **The app in 16 languages.** Every menu, dialog and the in-game panel follow your phone's language: English (US and UK), Japanese, French (France and Canada), German, Italian, Spanish (Spain and Latin America), Dutch, Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), Russian, Korean and Chinese (Simplified and Traditional). To use another one, pick it in **Settings › Interface › App language** (or in Android's own app language setting).
- **Controller navigation.** In the library, with a game selected: **A** plays it, **Y** opens its Game settings, **L / R** switch tabs. Buttons follow the Nintendo layout (A right, B bottom) by default; **Settings › Interface** keeps the Xbox layout if you prefer it.

- **HD cutscenes from your own video.** If you have your own HD copy of Awakening's anime cutscenes, such as a rip of the *Fire Emblem: HD Movie Collection* Blu-ray or another recording, ExaltDS can play your HD version in place of the game's 400×240 movies. The 3D cutscenes stay as they are.
  - **Nothing is included.** This release contains no HD cutscenes, video files or pictures from the game. ExaltDS only uses the video you choose and your own game file.
  - **How the import works:** in the sidebar, open **Mods / textures**, choose **HD movies from your video…** and pick the video file.
    - ExaltDS decodes the game's own movies from your copy and searches your video for each of the 14.
    - It finds where each one starts, any black bars, how the picture is framed, the frame rate and the brightness, then matches it to the game frame by frame.
    - It then renders the matched frames into HD clips on your device, with the device's own video encoder, and checks each clip.
    - On the AYN Thor this took about 8 minutes for a 15-minute video, with all 14 movies found and 99% of frames in HD. Then use **Apply and restart**.

# Nimbus Alpha 2.2.2 for Android

A second hotfix for Android. Linux and Windows stay on 2.2.1.

- **Phones that still showed "Nimbus could not start graphics" on 2.2.1** (for example some Helio G99 phones on Android 14) now start their games. On these phones Nimbus uses a second graphics path.
- Heads up: the second graphics path is slower than Vulkan, so games on those phones may run slower. Every other device stays on Vulkan.
- Every other device runs exactly as on 2.2.1.

## Good to know

- After updating, Nimbus prepares its shaders once more on the first start.
- Online play is unchanged: 2.2.2 on Android plays with 2.2, 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 on every platform.

## Updating

Install the 2.2.2 APK over 2.2 or 2.2.1. It updates in place and keeps your links and saves. Do not uninstall first.

Thanks to Velkooky on Reddit for finding and reporting this bug.

The headline: the graphics translation makes simpler shaders, so the GPU does less work for every picture.

- **Lighter shaders.** Many of the game's shaders look up numbers they could know in advance. The translation now works those out once and builds them into the shader. On our test device the GPU did 5-9% less work per frame. Without a frame rate limit, that gave 4-6% more frames in the open world.
- **Shaders are made once more after this update.** Because the shaders change, the first play after updating rebuilds them, so expect short hitches in new places for a while. To avoid them, run **Prepare shaders** again from the start screen.

The headline: the slabs over Gerudo Town are gone, and motion at the frame rate limit is steadier, with and without frame generation.

- **Gerudo Town slabs fixed.** After a visit to the Depths, huge slabs of terrain could hang over Gerudo Town. The ground there is built from a map the game draws in parts; the undrawn parts now hold what the game expects instead of leftovers from other images.
- **Steadier 60 without frame generation.** Each picture now lands on the screen's refresh grid, so camera pans no longer mix pictures held for one and three refreshes. On our test device the uneven pictures in a fast pan dropped from 4-6% to under 0.1%, for a few milliseconds of extra input lag.
- **No seam at the screen edge with Homemade frame generation.** While panning, a vertical seam could show a short way in from the edge of generated pictures, where new scenery enters the view.

Pagurin catches up with nx2android's main branch of 2026-11-17. Three new settings, an audio output picker in the game's pause menu, and Android's Performance Game Mode.

## What's new

- Three settings for each game. Under Input, Menu button shows or hides the on-screen menu button (Back still opens the menu), and Controllers either gives each controller its own player or makes them all player 1. Under Performance, GPU turbo holds the GPU at its highest clock, always or only while frames run late.
- The pause menu's Game tab has an Audio output row. It sends the game's sound to the output you pick, such as the device speaker or Bluetooth headphones, until the game ends.
- Pagurin declares Android's Performance Game Mode. With Pagurin set to Performance, a game keeps its own frame rate instead of stepping down to 40 or 30.
- A game added with the import tool while Pagurin is open now shows its new settings and size right away. In 0.2.1 you had to reopen Pagurin.
- The group headings in a game's settings (Graphics, Input, Performance and so on) are in the app's accent colour, so the groups stand apart.
- The README is reorganised, with a Quick start first.

## Before you update

releases.name: Pagurin 0.2.1
releases.body:
Pagurin catches up with nx2android's main branch of 2026-11-11: games can use local play over Wi-Fi, and a controller's face buttons can follow their labels.

## What's new

- **Local play over Wi-Fi.** Pagurin now has the network permissions a port's host asks for, so a game whose profile turns on local play (`DM_LAN`, such as Animal Crossing: New Horizons) can reach other players on the same Wi-Fi.
- **Face buttons setting.** A game's Input settings have a **Face buttons** row: **Position** (the Switch's layout, the default) or **Label** (A is the button marked A, as on an Xbox-style controller). It's the same setting as the pause menu's Face buttons row.
- **The import tool cleans up `sysdata/` too.** A port made with `--firmware` carries system data, and running the tool again now removes what an older port left there.

## Before you update

- The Face buttons row only shows for a port made from nx2android's main branch on 2026-11-09 or later. An older port doesn't read the setting, so the row stays hidden.

releases.name: Pagurin 0.2.0
releases.body:
GPU drivers now work the way nx2android's main branch takes them, and a game can be removed from the library.

## What's new

- **GPU drivers for nx2android's main branch.** Each game picks one of three:
  - **The game's own driver** (the default): the one its port was made with (`porter port --vulkan-driver`), or the system's if the port has none.
  - **The system driver**, even for a port that brought its own.
  - **A driver you added from a file.** Pagurin carries libadrenotools itself, so this also works for ports made without a driver.
- **Remove a game** from its settings tab. You choose whether to keep its save; a kept save is picked up again if you add the game back.
- **The import tool cleans up.** Running it again removes files an older port of the game left behind in `host/`, `mods/`, `RomFS/` and `aoc/`.
- The game page shows its button hints in the same order on every tab. LB and RB are on the tab bar.

## Before you update

- Choosing a driver needs a port made from nx2android's main branch on 2026-11-03 or later. An older port still runs, on the system's driver. Port it again to choose a driver.

releases.name: Pagurin 0.1.0
releases.body:
The first release. Pagurin keeps your Android ports of games from other platforms in one app, such as those made with [nx2android](https://github.com/shirai91/nx2android), instead of a separate app per game.

## What's in it

- A library of your ports, with search and sorting.
- Settings for each game: docked or handheld mode, the on-screen gamepad, rumble, the frame rate counter and the engine's performance switches. A game only shows the settings its own host reads.
- One game language for every game. A game that doesn't have it runs in English.
- GPU drivers, added from a file and picked per game.
- Save export, import and delete. Import also takes another app's save folder or a zip.
- Games added from a PC with the import tool, or moved over from ports already installed as their own apps (AYN devices, or Shizuku elsewhere).

## Downloads

| File | What it is |
|---|---|

失败点：clean 安装后重新移植《双人成行》时，`build_ipa_from_nsp.py` 的 `split_shaders()` 去读
`dm/games/010092A0172E4000/shader_map.tsv`，但该档案只有 `game.tsv` 和 `android.tsv`，文件不存在。

旧端口能跑，是因为旧端口目录里已有之前生成的 shader 表；clean 安装没有这些表，于是暴露了
“两文件档案被当成完整档案”的分支错误。

修复（提交 `70f4e38`）：档案缺表时禁用包复用，先把本次 shader split 生成的
`shader_map.tsv`、`shader_facts.tsv`、`shader_pairs.tsv` 写进本次档案副本，再继续后续步骤；
表齐全时才做数据行比对。
